meta.title: Old Rackets Found in School Closet

paragraphs: Old Rackets Found in School Closet. By Lily and May, with photos by Mia. On Thursday, the Explorers found twelve old badminton rackets in a closet behind the school hall. The door was shut for many years, and the closet was very dusty. The school cleaner gave Teacher Kim a small key, and she opened the door. The Explorers wanted to clean the closet before the school fair. Everybody was surprised by what was inside. Lily wrote this story for Explorers' Blog.

Inside, the children saw a pile of boxes. Dust was on every box. One box had twelve rackets, and each racket had a green handle. Another box had a net with blue and white stripes. The rackets were old, but only two of them were broken. Mia took photos of everything, and Leo made a list of the equipment. The boxes were heavy, so two children carried each one. The old boxes were put on a table in the hall. The closet was cleaned in one hour.

At the bottom of the last box, May found an old document. It was a list of names, and the title was "School Sports Club." May read the names, and the Explorers listened. The paper was yellow, and the writing was blue. It was only one page. Nobody knows the date, and the names are not the names of children in our school today. Teacher Kim put the document in a clear folder, and it is now in the school library. Teacher Kim took a photo of the empty closet.

After the club hour, Coach Matt looked at the rackets. "Ten of them are good," he said. He hit a ball up and down with each racket. Coach Matt says that a local shop can fix the two broken rackets. The handles are clean now. He also says that the net is strong, and the stripes are still bright.

The Explorers have a plan for a new activity. At the school fair, children can play badminton on the field with the old rackets. It will be a fun morning. Leo and Coach Matt will put up the net between two trees. Teacher Kim says that every child can try, and nobody needs a racket from home. Do you have an old thing at home that other children may enjoy? Tell us in a message!
